title: The universe's most common state
question: What is plasma, and why does it matter so much?
hook: Rare on Earth, it makes up nearly all of the ordinary matter in the universe.
idea: Plasma is an ionized, electrically conductive state of matter that dominates the universe even though it is rarely encountered on Earth.

beats.prompt: A neutral gas is heated strongly until a significant portion of its particles become charged. How does it behave?

choices.label: It stays a poor conductor because it is still a gas
choices.feedback: Once a significant portion of particles is charged, the gas has become plasma, and charged particles make it conductive.

choices.label: It turns into a solid
choices.feedback: Plasma is the fourth state, not a route to solid; its charged particles keep it fluid and conductive.

beats.explain: Heating a neutral gas can ionize it, and the charged particles in the resulting plasma make it electrically conductive.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the history of plasma in order.
items: Faraday investigates glow discharge in rarefied gases (1831)
Crookes presents the idea of a fourth state of matter (1879)
beats.explain: The arc came first in 1803, then Faraday in 1831, Crookes in 1879, and Langmuir in the 1920s.

beats.prompt: Sort each into found in nature or used in technology.
beats.explain: Stars and lightning are natural plasmas, while televisions, etching, and fusion energy use plasma's response to electromagnetic fields.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Plasma is made when a gas is ionized.
So it contains charged particles, ions and electrons.
Its overall charge is roughly zero.
Therefore plasma cannot respond to electric fields.
beats.explain: Although the overall charge is roughly zero, its charged particles make plasma very sensitive to externally applied fields.
